artworks.title: Circe Invidiosa
artworks.description: Waterhouse paints Circe poisoning the bay for Scylla — the jealous revenge that answers Glaucus' refusal. The sea-god himself is off-canvas, but the green pour is the climax of his Ovidian love story (Art Gallery of South Australia).

artworks.title: Glaucus and Scylla
artworks.description: Turner's late oil dissolves Ovid's sea-chase into light and spray: Glaucus, the blue-green fisherman-god, pursues Scylla across a boiling gulf while Circe's jealousy waits offstage. The painting (once at the Kimbell) is among the most famous modern images of the Anthedonian sea-god's doomed love.

artworks.title: Glaucus and Scylla
artworks.description: Mannerist panel in the Kunsthistorisches Museum, Vienna (GG 2615): Spranger gives Glaucus a muscular sea-god's body as he reaches for the fleeing nymph Scylla, the Ovidian pursuit that Circe will answer with poison. Prague court taste made the Anthedonian fisherman a glamorous marine lover.

artworks.title: Glaucus and Scylla
artworks.description: Rosa's dark coastal drama: the transformed Glaucus, still half wild after the herb, stretches toward Scylla on a rocky shore while the sea behind them promises Circe's revenge. The painting keeps Ovid's Metamorphoses as a storm of desire rather than a polite mythological idyll.

artworks.title: Glaucus and Scylla
artworks.description: French classical canvas at the J. Paul Getty Museum (84.PA.13): La Hyre stages Glaucus' plea to Scylla with cool clarity — the sea-god's blue flesh and the nymph's recoil before Circe ruins the strait. It is one of the cleanest seventeenth-century readings of the Anthedonian love story.

music.title: Scylla et Glaucus
music.description: Leclair's tragédie en musique gives the Anthedonian sea-god the title role — Glaucus, Scylla, and Circe's revenge for the Paris Opéra.

popCulture.title: Metamorphoses
popCulture.creator: Ovid
popCulture.description: Books 13–14: the fisherman tastes the herb, becomes a blue-green god, loves Scylla, and watches Circe poison the strait.

popCulture.title: Glaucus
popCulture.description: Semi-divine sea-dweller of Anthedon — distinct from the Lycian captain, forever bound to Scylla's transformation.
